skill.name: Comma between a dependent and a main clause
skill.why: The comma shows readers where the 'if' part stops and the main part starts.
skill.how: Starts with when, if, because or although? Put a comma where that part ends.

beats.say: Some sentences start with a part that can't stand alone.
That's a dependent clause. It leans on the main part.
Put a comma where the dependent clause ends.
beats.show: When the bell rang**,** we ran.

beats.say: Miss it, and the crew seems to eat the yeti!
beats.show: While the crew ate the yeti watched.

beats.say: Comma in. Now the yeti is just watching.
beats.show: While the crew ate**,** the yeti watched.

weDo.hint: Find the part that can't stand alone. Where does it end?
weDo.success: 'When the snow stopped' can't stand alone. The comma goes where it ends, before 'we'.

options.text: When the snow stopped, we built a fort.
When the snow stopped we, built a fort.
options.reason: The comma splits 'we' from what we did. It goes after 'stopped'.

options.text: When the snow stopped. We built a fort.
options.reason: 'When the snow stopped.' can't stand alone, so it can't be a sentence.

weDo.prompt: Which version is punctuated so the penguin is safe?
weDo.hint: Read each one aloud. Is anyone cooking the penguin?
weDo.success: The comma after 'cooking' ends the dependent clause. Mo cooks, and the penguin just dances.

options.text: While Mo was cooking, the penguin danced.
While Mo was cooking the penguin danced.
options.reason: With no comma, it first reads as if Mo was cooking the penguin!

options.text: While Mo was cooking the penguin, danced.
options.reason: Now Mo really is cooking the penguin, and 'danced' has no doer.
